steps.procedure: 1. Release the pressure that remains in the hydraulic tank and piping to examine. For details, see Testing and Adjusting, “Release Remained Pressure in Hydraulic Circuit”. 2. Are the control valve body and the arm spool clean, with no twisting, seizure, scratches, or dirt? (They must move smoothly and not be stuck.) REMARK Be careful that dirt does not enter during recovery work.

branches.YES: • Arm control valve body and spool are normal. • Go to the next check item.
branches.NO: • Arm control valve body and spool are defective. • Repair or replace the arm control valve body and spool. • Go to “Confirmation of repair”.

steps.cause: Pressure compensation valve on IN side of arm control valve
steps.procedure: 1. Examine it. For details, see Testing and Adjusting, “Examine and Adjust Oil Pressure in Work Equipment, Swing, and Travel Circuits”. 2. Does the troubleshooting result of the main relief pressure agree with the judgment criteria? 3. Do relief of other work equipment and examine. 4. Is the arm stopped? 5. Interchange the pressure compensation valves on IN and OUT sides of arm control valve, and examine. 6. Is there no change, and does the phenomenon reproduce? REMARK The area ratios of the pressure compensation valves on the IN side and OUT sides are different. Be sure to set them back to their initial positions after troubleshooting.
